newsitem.title: USA: Canada LPGs lower amid weak demand, industry meet.
newsitem.headline: Canada LPGs lower amid weak demand, industry meet.

text.p: Canadian liquefied petroleum gas prices (LPG) were lower this week, under pressure from weak demand and lower U.S. values, players said Thursday.
Prices in the last week have fallen in the U.S. Gulf Coast due to a lack in demand and a sell-off of propane by a major with a long position.
Canadian traders said demand was beginning to slacken as spring approached although activity appeared less than year-ago levels.
In the eastern hub of Sarnia, spot propane tumbled 2.25 cents from last Thursday, particularly following a drop in posting prices by about 1 cent to 1.50 cents earlier today.
Propane was assessed between 37.25 cents and 37.50 cents a gallon with activity dampened by an industry event in Atlanta, Georgia.
Western players at Edomonton hub pegged prices a tad lower at 30.00/32.00 cents, finding some support in residential demand.
The butane markets were also assessed lower and quiet, following the fall in U.S. Mont Belvieu, Texas, and Conway, Kansas.
